findings.issue: Self-disclosed deviation #2 (CONTACT_EMAIL=${CONTACT_EMAIL:-} instead of the spec's literal CONTACT_EMAIL=${CONTACT_EMAIL}) is justified in the implementer's reasoning by a failure mode that does not actually occur. The env: block always defines the CONTACT_EMAIL key on the Deploy step (CONTACT_EMAIL: ${{ secrets.CONTACT_EMAIL }} at line ~109) regardless of whether the underlying GitHub secret exists — a nonexistent secrets.X reference evaluates to an empty string during expression evaluation, it does not omit the key. appleboy/ssh-action's envs: allowlist then exports CONTACT_EMAIL as a defined-but-empty shell variable on the remote session. Under `set -euo pipefail`, `set -u` only errors on a variable that was never assigned — 'defined but empty' does not trigger 'unbound variable'. So a bare ${CONTACT_EMAIL} in the heredoc would NOT abort the deploy in the scenario described (secret not yet created). Independently verified this matches the parallel security-auditor's targeted_check_results.4_contact_email_fallback_deviation conclusion.
findings.impact: The actual code change is harmless (CONTACT_EMAIL legitimately defaults to empty per config.go:83, and no other var in the heredoc shares this treatment, so nothing else is masked). The problem is purely that the written justification for the deviation is factually wrong. If this incorrect claim is copied into decisions.md as-is, it misleads future maintainers about how appleboy/ssh-action + set -u actually behave, and could lead someone to defensively add :- fallbacks to every var in the heredoc 'just in case', which actually would be harmful for vars like DB_PASSWORD or DB_HOST where silently defaulting to empty is unsafe.
findings.recommendation: Keep the code as-is (the :- fallback is harmless and mildly defensive), but correct the rationale before it lands in decisions.md: state plainly that the deviation is not load-bearing against the 'secret not yet created' scenario, and that it's kept only as an intentional, narrowly-scoped defensive default consistent with config.go's own empty-string default for this specific var — not a general pattern to replicate for other heredoc vars.

findings.issue: No concurrency block, and the on: block triggers both push (branches: ["**"]) and pull_request. For every commit pushed to a branch that has an open PR, both events fire for the same commit, producing two full, redundant runs of go-test (each spinning up its own mariadb:11.4 service container and running the whole Go suite twice).
findings.impact: Doubles CI minutes/cost on every push to an open PR branch. Not a correctness bug — both runs will report the same pass/fail result — but it's a measurable, avoidable waste that will scale with PR volume. The implementer's stated reason for omitting concurrency (avoiding cancellation of the tag-triggered, deploy-gating run) is a real and valid concern for a naively-scoped concurrency group, but doesn't actually require omitting concurrency entirely.
findings.recommendation: Add a concurrency group scoped to include github.event_name (or restrict the push trigger's branches to just the default branch, e.g. branches: [main], since pull_request already covers feature-branch feedback), e.g.: `concurrency: { group: test-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true }`. Keying on event_name keeps the workflow_call invocation from deploy.yml (tag push, different event/ref) in its own group, so it can never be cancelled by a PR-branch push/pull_request pair colliding in the same group.

findings.issue: The CI-only MariaDB root password "ci_root" is a literal repeated in three separate places: job-level env (line 24), service-level env (line 30), and the --health-cmd string inside options: (line 46). GitHub Actions does not expose the env context inside jobs.<job_id>.services.<service_id>.options (confirmed: this field only has access to github/needs/strategy/matrix/secrets/inputs, not env), so the third occurrence can't be replaced with an expression referencing the other two — this is a real platform constraint, not an oversight, but the duplication across all three still has to be kept in sync by hand.
findings.impact: If a future edit rotates the value in the env blocks but misses the options: string (or vice versa), the health-cmd check will authenticate with the wrong password and fail every retry, timing out the service container and failing the job before any test runs. This fails loudly (job never gets past service startup) rather than silently, so the blast radius is limited to wasted debugging time, not a silent gap in coverage.
findings.recommendation: No code change required given the GHA constraint; consider adding an inline comment at the options: line noting the value must be kept in sync with the env: blocks above it if changed, since there is no way to express that dependency structurally.

Push-trigger deviation (self-disclosed #3, part 1): confirmed GitHub Actions push.branches filters only match refs/heads/* — a tag push (refs/tags/*) does not trigger a workflow whose push trigger declares only branches: (no tags: key), regardless of the branches pattern's content. branches: ["**"] therefore correctly excludes tag pushes, avoiding the described double-run of go-test on a tagged push (once standalone, once via workflow_call from deploy.yml).

All four touched/new YAML files (test.yml, deploy.yml, docker-compose.yml, docker-compose.prod.yml) parse cleanly via python3 yaml.safe_load.

clean_check: This task is CI/CD-and-infra-config-only with no application code changes, so dimensions 5 (type safety), 6 (unit testing of business logic), and 11 (resource management/heavy singletons) don't apply. Focused effort went into dimension 10 (cross-file consistency — the five-hop CONTACT_EMAIL chain, the nginx proxy swap mirrored across two files, and the migration-replication logic mirrored from migrate.go) and dimension 1/2 (architecture — the reusable-workflow wiring between test.yml and deploy.yml). All three of the implementer's self-disclosed deviations were independently re-derived from first principles (GitHub Actions context/trigger semantics, bash set -u semantics, migrate.go's actual sort/glob logic) rather than taken on faith, and one (the CONTACT_EMAIL :- fallback) was found to rest on an incorrect technical justification, which is reported as a minor finding even though the resulting code is harmless.
summary: 0 critical, 0 major, 3 minor findings. All five CONTACT_EMAIL hops, both nginx proxy swaps, the reusable test.yml/deploy.yml wiring, the migration-replication step, and the push-trigger tag-dedup logic hold up under independent verification (env/envs congruence checked programmatically at 28/28, both nginx configs pass `nginx -t`, migration glob/sort logic matches migrate.go exactly, GHA context syntax for job.services.<id>.id confirmed valid). The three minor findings are: an incorrect (though harmless) technical justification documented for the CONTACT_EMAIL :- deviation, a real but deliberately-accepted CI cost from missing concurrency dedup on PR branches, and an unavoidable (GHA-platform-forced) triplication of a throwaway CI password literal. None block merge on their own; none carry a security or functional-correctness consequence in production.
